La documentación de esta integración la escribe su autor y, por ahora, solo está disponible en inglés.

Control your Becker roller shutters, venetian blinds, screens, awnings and sun
sails (Centronic, CentronicPLUS and B-Tronic radio) through your **CentralControl
CC31, CC41 or CC51**, and read its sun, wind, rain and temperature sensors, from
Gladys. Everything stays on your local network: the integration talks to the
JSON-RPC API of the box (`http://<box>/cgi-bin/cc51rpc.cgi`), never to the
Becker cloud nor its relay.

> This integration has **never been tested with a real box yet**: it was built
> from Becker's own Home Assistant integration (becker_centralcontrol_has, MIT)
> and tested against a simulated box. Unofficial, not affiliated with
> Becker-Antriebe GmbH.

## Configuration

1. Give your CentralControl a fixed address in your router (DHCP reservation).
2. In the integration's Configuration tab, enter that address (like
   `192.168.1.70`; add `:port` if the box answers on another port than 80).
   Names in `.local` do not resolve in the container: use the IP address.
3. Optionally change the read interval (60 s by default, 30 s to 1 h) and the
   language of the feature names.
4. Save, then **Test the connection**: it lists the covers the box answers with.
5. Add your covers and sensors from the **Discovery** tab.

## What you get

- **Each cover** (shutter, venetian, screen, awning, sun sail, blinds,
  fold-out shutter) becomes a shutter with an **Open / close** feature (open,
  close, stop). When the motor sends its position back (B-Tronic,
  CentronicPLUS: "feedback" in the box), a **Position** feature (0 % closed,
  100 % open) is read at every interval and can be set. Centronic motors give
  no state back: only the commands, never a position.
- An **awning** is reversed, as in Becker's integration: "close" retracts it,
  and its position is the one the box gives.
- **Each sensor** (sun, wind, rain, twilight, temperature) becomes a read-only
  sensor. Sun and twilight are levels 0 to 15, wind a level 0 to 11 (the
  sensor's own scale, not km/h), rain 0 (dry) or 1 (rain), temperature in °C.
  A value outside these ranges is not published.
- Doors, garage doors, roof and tilt windows, lights, switches, heating and
  scenes of the box are not offered in this version.

## The stop

The **stop** is never blocked: not by a read in progress (it cuts it), not by a
pause asked by the box, not by another command waiting, not by the list of the
box not yet read, not by a configuration that cannot be read (it goes to the
last address known), not by `/data` being slow or unreadable. It leaves at once
and waits up to 3.3 s for the answer (a slow answer is an answer); when the
connection itself fails, it is written again every 250 ms within those 3.3 s.
**Any answer of the box counts** (an acceptance, a refusal, an error page);
a 429 or 5xx, a timeout or a cut connection does not.

The stop is kept (in memory, and in `/data` without waiting for it) until a read
of the cover, started after the box answered, shows it no longer moves:

- a stop the box has not answered is sent again after 5 s, 10 s, 20 s, 30 s,
  then every minute and at each successful read, **without end and without age
  limit**: only an answered send counts as a try;
- a stop the box answered without accepting it (a refusal, an error page) is
  acked as failed, and the read back decides as for an accepted one;
- the read back waits for the end of a pause the box asked (429, 5xx); when it
  gets no answer it is tried again after 5 s, 10 s, 20 s... up to every minute;
  when the box refuses to give that state (a group removed), the stop ends;
- answered but the cover still moves the same way: sent again, **3 answered
  tries at most**, then shown "still moving" on the badge;
- the cover moves **the other way**: a move started elsewhere (app, remote) is
  left alone;
- a motor without feedback, or a box that does not say whether it moves: one
  answered stop is all there is;
- a **newer command** of that cover (open, close, position) accepted by the box
  replaces the stop; a newer command without answer does not (the stop goes);
- after a restart, the stops kept in `/data` leave at once, before Gladys is
  reached.

A stop is not sent only while **no address of the box is known at all** (never
configured, nothing in `/data`): it is kept and leaves as soon as an address is
saved. Clicking stop also drops the commands of that cover not yet sent: nothing
clicked before a stop leaves after it.

## The close

**Close** follows the same path (ahead of everything, cuts the reads, not held
by a pause, by the list not yet read, by a new address not confirmed yet, 3.3 s
budget), but it is never sent again after a restart. Its direction comes from
the type the box lists now, else the type the device was created with, else a
shutter (down). It is refused only when the box lists that id as something
else than a cover (a door, a light).

## Open and position

They are refused, with the reason on the device's badge, when: the
configuration is not valid; the box asked to slow down (429, 5xx; the pause is
kept across a restart, 1 min to 6 h); the cover has not been listed by the box
since the start (or since it stopped answering); the box lists that id with
another type; the address of the box changed and was not confirmed yet; the
motor gives no position (position only); the value is not a whole number from 0
to 100; 32 commands already wait; the command cannot leave within 2.5 s (its
answer is awaited until 3.5 s); or a stop or close of that cover came after it.

**A new address of the box**: another box may hold covers with the same ids and
types. After the address changes, only stop and close go until you press **Test
the connection** and the box answers (kept across a restart).

Several covers move at once (up to 8; a scene of five covers sets all five).
If a command gets no answer while others are in flight, the box may serve one
request at a time: the covers are then commanded one after the other until the
integration restarts; in that mode a command may leave until 3.8 s and is
answered until 4.7 s, so that a scene of five covers at 0.9 s each still sets
all five (the first scene, which finds out, may see the last two unanswered).
On such a box a stop may also wait behind a command the box is serving. A command is
said **applied** only when a read after it shows the asked position (5 s and
20 s after); otherwise the badge says "accepted, waiting for the read back",
"not applied yet", "sent, without confirmation" (no answer) or "nothing sent".

## Reads

The positions and sensors are read at the interval you set, one request at a
time; the lists of the box every 10 minutes. A cover missing from one list
(the box may list part of its items) is kept until the next list, read at the
next read; missing twice, it is shown "no longer listed". When every cover read
fails, the integration is not shown connected and each cover says "Not read". A
read that left before a command
of a cover is never applied after it, and reads apply in the order they left. A
cover or the sensor list that fails never stops the others. A restart (same box) never reads the states sooner than the interval; the lists
(two requests) are read at once, so open and position work right after it.

## Troubleshooting

- **"not yet read back from the box"**: the box was not listed yet in this
  session (unreachable at start); press Test the connection: once it answers,
  the covers are known.
- **"another type of cover"**: the id of that device now holds another cover in
  the box (reconfigured). Delete the device and add it again from Discovery.
- **"/data not read yet"**: the file `/data/becker-state.json` could not be
  read (or took more than 2 s); it is left as it is, read again every 30 s, and
  the stops it keeps are sent as soon as it is read. Nothing is written to it
  meanwhile, so the stops are not kept across a restart until then.
- The logs never hold an address you typed by mistake.

## Parámetros de configuración

Estos son los parámetros que Becker CentralControl te pide en su pantalla de configuración en Gladys.

| Parámetro | Tipo | Obligatorio | Descripción |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your Becker covers in Gladys | `section` | No | Each shutter, venetian blind, screen, awning or sun sail set up in your CentralControl CC31, CC41 or CC51 (Centronic, CentronicPLUS, B-Tronic) becomes a shutter in the Discovery tab (open, close, stop, and the position when the motor gives it back), and each sun, wind, rain or temperature sensor a read-only sensor. Everything stays on your local network (the JSON-RPC API of the box), no Becker cloud. The stop is never blocked. Never tested with a real box yet. Unofficial, not affiliated with Becker-Antriebe. |
| Address of the CentralControl | `string` | Sí | The local IP address of your CentralControl, like 192.168.1.70 (port 80 unless you add another one, like 192.168.1.70:8080). Give it a fixed address in your router (DHCP reservation). |
| Read interval (s) | `number` | No | How often the positions and the sensors are read from the box (30 to 3600 s). |
| Language of the feature names | `select` | No | Used for the names of the features of the devices added from now on. |

## Cómo instalar Becker CentralControl en Gladys

1. En Gladys, abre **Integraciones**: Becker CentralControl aparece en el catálogo junto a las integraciones nativas, con una insignia de comunidad.
2. Haz clic en **Instalar**. Gladys descarga la imagen Docker (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-becker:0.1.1`), la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo y genera la interfaz de la integración (dispositivos, descubrimiento y configuración).
3. Abre la pantalla de **Configuración** de la integración, rellena los parámetros y guarda.
4. También puedes instalarla directamente desde la URL de su repositorio: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-becker](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-becker).

Becker CentralControl requiere Gladys `>=5.1.0`. El catálogo de Gladys se actualiza cada hora, así que una nueva versión está disponible como máximo una hora después de publicarse.

¿Todavía no usas Gladys? Es gratuito y de código abierto: [sigue la guía de instalación](/es/docs/) para empezar.

## Sobre las integraciones externas

Becker CentralControl es una **integración externa**: una integración comunitaria empaquetada como contenedor Docker y publicada en GitHub. Gladys la instala con un clic y la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo. La publica y mantiene [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7), no el equipo principal de Gladys.
